chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the redness disappears from this side, meaning the direction of the east, then the sun has set in the east of the earth and its west.'

key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: The redness or glow of reddish hue remaining in the sky after sunset
key_terms.الْمَشْرِقِ: The east, the direction of sunrise

ai.seo_question: How to determine the exact time for breaking the fast according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the precise moment for iftar by linking the disappearance of the sunset's redness (shuruq al-shams) to the actual setting of the sun, a key criterion in Shia fiqh for determining Maghrib prayer time. It reflects the scholarly understanding that the visual cue of fading redness serves as a reliable indicator that the sun has dipped below the horizon globally, ensuring the fast is broken at the correct astronomical moment.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bi Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Qasim Ibn Urwat, from Bureyd Bin MUawiya who said,
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When the redness disappears from this side, meaning the direction of the east, so the sun has disappeared in the east of the earth and its west’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and a number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from Burayd ibn Mu‘awiyah who has said the following: “I once heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘When the redness disappears from this side (the east), it is sunset all over the east and west of the earth (land).”’
